chunks: Ḥukaym ibn Dāwūd ibn Ḥukaym narrated to me from Salamah, who said: Ayyūb ibn Sulaymān ibn Ayyūb Al-Fazārī narrated to me from ‘Alī ibn Ḥazawwar, who said: I heard Laylā, and she was saying:

I heard the lamentation of the Jinn over al-Ḥusayn ibn ‘Alī (peace be upon him), and she was reciting: O eyes! Shed abundant tears, for verily the grieved one cries with agony and anguish. O eyes! Do not let the comfort of sleep distract you from remembering the family of Muḥammad (peace be upon them) and their anguish. Their bodies remained for three nights on the desert ground among the beasts, and all of them were martyred.
ai.seo_question: What did the Jinn say about the martyrdom of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.)?
ai.summary: This narration from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the cosmic scale of Karbala by depicting Jinn mourning the Ahl al-Bayt, thereby validating the event's significance beyond human witnesses. The specific detail of bodies remaining exposed among beasts for three days aligns with historical accounts of the Battle of Karbala, emphasizing the humiliation inflicted upon the Prophet’s family. This lamentation serves as a foundational text for Shia devotional practices, reinforcing the emotional and spiritual connection to Imam Husayn’s sacrifice.
